name: How long does a garage conversion take from plans to final inspection?

mainEntity.name: How long does a garage conversion usually take in Los Angeles from design and permits to completion?
mainEntity.text: How long does a garage conversion usually take in Los Angeles from design and permits to completion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timelines are often longer than homeowners expect because the project has two separate phases: preconstruction and buildout. Preconstruction includes feasibility checks, measuring the existing structure, preparing plans, engineering, submitting permits, and responding to corrections. Construction then starts after approval and can move quickly if the garage shell is in good condition and utility runs are straightforward. Delays usually come from plan check corrections, structural repairs, upgrading the electrical panel, trenching for plumbing, or waiting on inspections. A basic conversion can move faster than a new detached ADU because the shell already exists, but a project with foundation work, roof repair, or major code corrections can take much longer. If the goal is a rental unit, schedule should also account for city inspections and utility sign-offs before occupancy. Homeowners should ask for a realistic start-to-finish timeline, not just the construction duration, because permitting often becomes the longest part of the process. The cleanest projects are usually those with a legally built garage, clear zoning, and minimal structural surprises.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion can take several months from first plans to final inspection, with permit review, revisions, construction, and utility coordination all affecting the schedule. Faster projects are usually simple conversions with limited structural work, while older garages and full ADUs take longer.
